md_name: X-ray Phase-Contrast Microscopy of Irradiated Epithelial Cells
md_description: This workflow describes cultured human epithelial cells exposed to ionizing radiation, followed by X-ray phase-contrast microscopy to record high-resolution structural images of organelles and cytoskeletal elements. The pipeline includes radiation treatment and sample preparation, image capture with X-ray source and microscope parameters recorded in the acquisition node, and computational image correction, correlation, and segmentation to generate quantitative structural outputs for studying radiation-induced damage and repair.

cultured_human_epithelial_cells.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the cultured human epithelial cells themselves: their biological identity, origin, culture background, and intrinsic starting state before any radiation or imaging. I excluded radiation dose, exposure conditions, microscope settings, file/image properties, and computed metrics because those belong to the downstream Process, Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided sample identifiers and experiment identifiers because those are generally root-level and should not be duplicated elsewhere. The fields below are limited to reusable identity and culture-origin metadata needed to interpret the starting material.

md_schema.descr: Name of the human epithelial cell line or primary epithelial population used as the starting material before radiation exposure; use the exact vendor or laboratory designation when available, e.g. 'HeLa', 'HaCaT', or a primary epithelial isolate name.
Biological species of the cultured cells at the time of experiment; record the organism from which the epithelial cells were derived, typically 'Homo sapiens'.
Anatomical tissue source from which the epithelial cells were derived before culture, if known; e.g. skin, lung, colon, or cervix.

Intrinsic culture state of the cells immediately before radiation exposure, describing whether they are immortalized, primary, differentiated, or stem-like; use the category that best matches the starting population.

Basic intrinsic growth phenotype of the cultured epithelial cells prior to perturbation, indicating whether the cells are adherent or suspension-growing; this reflects the cell model rather than any procedure performed during the workflow.

ionizing_radiation_exposure.reasoning: This Process node should capture how the radiation perturbation was performed: the radiation modality, dose, rate, exposure geometry, duration, and the source system used. I excluded cell identity/origin fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded imaging or file-output details because those belong downstream to Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided derived biological outcomes, since this node describes the experimental treatment operation, not its consequences. No previously generated fields were repeated.

md_schema.descr: Type of ionizing radiation applied to the cells during the exposure process; record the modality used in this experiment, for example X-ray, gamma, or electron beam.

Delivered ionizing radiation dose to the cell culture during exposure, measured in gray (Gy) at the time of treatment; report the nominal or calibrated dose per sample, typically within a range of 0 to 20 Gy for cellular irradiation experiments.

Radiation dose rate during exposure, expressed in gray per minute (Gy/min); record the calibrated delivery rate used for the sample at the time of treatment, typically spanning low-dose-rate to high-dose-rate exposures.

Total duration of the radiation exposure step in minutes, measured from the start to the end of irradiation for the cell sample; use the actual treatment interval, typically from seconds to several minutes depending on dose rate.
Distance between the radiation source or beam exit and the cell sample during exposure, in millimeters (mm); record the geometry used for dose delivery and field uniformity, if applicable.
Configuration of the sample relative to the radiation beam during exposure, describing how the culture was positioned for treatment.

Hardware system used to deliver the ionizing radiation exposure, including manufacturer, model, and serial number when available; this is the active agent for the Process node and should identify the source used for dose delivery.

Temperature of the cell sample during radiation exposure, measured at the treatment point in degrees Celsius; record the controlled temperature if the exposure was performed outside standard incubator conditions, typically around 20 to 37 C.

irradiated_cell_culture.reasoning: This Entity node should describe the irradiated cell culture as the post-treatment biological sample: its status after radiation exposure, any recovered or fixed preparation state, and the dose history carried forward from the upstream process. I excluded microscope settings, image file properties, and downstream analysis outputs because those belong to Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating the upstream radiation process parameters except where they are needed as intrinsic sample provenance for the treated culture. No already_generated fields were repeated or paraphrased as new fields.

md_schema.descr: Biological state of the epithelial culture after completion of the ionizing radiation exposure and before X-ray microscopy; use this to indicate whether the sample was immediately imaged, recovered, fixed, or otherwise prepared after treatment.

Elapsed time in minutes between the end of radiation exposure and the start of the X-ray microscopy preparation or imaging step; record the actual interval for this treated culture, typically from 0 minutes for immediate imaging to longer recovery periods.

Cumulative ionizing radiation dose carried by this treated cell culture, expressed in gray (Gy); report the delivered dose associated with the sample after exposure, typically within the range used in the experiment.

Identifier for the repeated exposure instance of this culture within the irradiation experiment, for example a replicate label such as 'rep1' or 'dose_5gy_a'; use a string that uniquely distinguishes treated cultures at the sample level.

Estimated cell culture confluence after irradiation and before microscopy, expressed as a percentage (%) of the available surface area covered by cells; record the observed culture density at the sample stage, typically 0 to 100.

xray_phase_contrast_microscopy.reasoning: This Capture node should capture the measurement session and instrument configuration: microscope identity, X-ray source settings, optics/detector configuration, sample mounting conditions, and exposure/acquisition settings that were actively controlled during imaging. I excluded sample provenance and radiation treatment details because those belong to upstream Entity/Process nodes, and I excluded file format, path, and image quality metrics because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided analysis outputs such as segmentation or correlation results, since those are downstream Derivative/Process territory. No already_generated fields were repeated.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the X-ray phase-contrast microscope used for image acquisition; record the hardware vendor responsible for the instrument in this imaging session.
Model name or number of the X-ray phase-contrast microscope used for acquisition; record the specific instrument configuration that produced the raw images.
Instrument serial number for the X-ray phase-contrast microscope, when available; use the exact hardware identifier assigned to the acquisition system.
Type of X-ray source used during phase-contrast microscopy, describing the active illumination system configured for the acquisition session.

Incident X-ray photon energy used for image acquisition, measured in kiloelectronvolts (keV) at the microscope during the capture session; report the configured energy, typically in the soft to hard X-ray range used for phase-contrast imaging.
Per-frame X-ray exposure time in milliseconds during the microscopy acquisition session; record the actual camera integration time used for each image or projection.
Detector or camera model used to record the X-ray phase-contrast images; include the specific sensor system attached to the microscope during acquisition.
Effective pixel size at the sample plane in micrometers (µm) for the acquired images; record the calibrated sampling resolution used during imaging, typically in the submicron to few-micron range.
Width of the imaged field of view in micrometers (µm) at the sample plane during acquisition; record the spatial coverage of each frame or stack slice.
Height of the imaged field of view in micrometers (µm) at the sample plane during acquisition; record the spatial coverage of each frame or stack slice.
Mounting configuration of the irradiated cell culture during X-ray imaging, such as on a slide, membrane, capillary, or chamber; record how the sample was physically positioned in the microscope.
Optical or phase-contrast configuration used during acquisition, including any objective, condenser, or phase optics settings relevant to the imaging session.
Acquisition mode used for X-ray phase-contrast imaging, indicating whether the session collected projection images, tomography, or another capture mode configured on the instrument.
Ambient or stage temperature during image acquisition in degrees Celsius, measured at the microscope during the capture session when temperature was actively controlled or monitored.

raw_xray_image_stack.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the raw data artifact itself: file format, dimensions, size, frame count, storage location, and basic technical quality flags. I excluded microscope configuration, exposure settings, and sample mounting details because those belong to the upstream Capture node. I also excluded correction, alignment, segmentation, and quantitative outputs because those are downstream Process and Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were repeated or semantically duplicated.

md_schema.descr: Digital file format of the raw phase-contrast image stack as stored after acquisition; record the actual format used for the unprocessed microscopy data, for example TIFF, CZI, HDF5, or DICOM.

Total size of the raw image stack file in bytes at the time of storage; record the archived size of the acquisition output, typically ranging from megabytes to gigabytes depending on image count and resolution.
Width of each raw image frame in pixels, measured from the stored image data; report the pixel dimension of the acquisition output at the time it was written.
Height of each raw image frame in pixels, measured from the stored image data; report the pixel dimension of the acquisition output at the time it was written.
Number of frames, slices, or projections contained in the raw X-ray image stack; record the total count present in the stored data object.
Per-pixel intensity precision of the raw image data, expressed as bits per pixel; record the native acquisition bit depth such as 8, 12, 16, or 32.
Whether the stored raw image stack was compressed at the file level when saved; use this to indicate the technical storage condition of the raw artifact.
Storage location or URI of the raw image stack file, for example a filesystem path, object-store URI, or database reference used to retrieve the raw data artifact.

Basic technical quality flag describing whether the raw image stack is usable, partially corrupted, or corrupted before any computational correction; assess this on the stored artifact, not from biological interpretation.

image_correction_and_correlation.reasoning: This Process node should describe the computational transformation applied to the raw images: software identity, version, repository, correction steps, registration/correlation method, and key algorithm parameters. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to the input Signal node, and I excluded corrected-image file attributes because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided segmentation and scientific interpretation outputs, since those are downstream Derivative territory. No already_generated fields were repeated or semantically duplicated.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to perform detector correction, alignment, and image correlation for this processing step; record the exact application used in the workflow.
Version of the image processing software used for correction and correlation; record the installed release or build that generated the processed images.

Repository, package source, or distribution location for the processing software; record the source used to identify or reproduce the software environment, such as a Git URL, package registry, or vendor site.
Method used to correct detector artifacts in the raw phase-contrast images during processing, such as flat-field correction, dark-current subtraction, bad-pixel replacement, or combined correction.
Registration or correlation method used to align phase-contrast images during processing, for example cross-correlation, feature-based registration, rigid alignment, or non-rigid alignment.
Index of the frame used as the reference for image alignment and correlation in this processing step; record the frame number or slice selected as the alignment anchor.
Number of optimization or refinement iterations performed during image alignment and correlation, measured for the processing run on the input stack.
Numeric threshold used to accept or terminate image correlation or registration during processing; record the value applied by the software, with the exact scale defined by the method implementation.
Number of channels or image channels retained after correction and correlation, if the processing step preserves multi-channel data; record the output channel count at the end of this process.

corrected_aligned_images.reasoning: This Signal node should describe the processed image artifact after correction and alignment: the stored file format, dimensions, size, frame count, and technical integrity/quality of the corrected output. I excluded software, algorithms, and registration parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded segmentation or quantitative structural measurements because those belong downstream to the Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any fields already generated for the raw image signal, unless the meaning here is specifically about the corrected output artifact.

md_schema.descr: Digital file format of the corrected and aligned image data as stored after processing; record the actual format used for the derived image artifact, for example TIFF, HDF5, or OME-TIFF.
Total size of the corrected and aligned image file in bytes at the time of storage; record the archived size of the processed artifact, typically dependent on frame count and resolution.
Width of each corrected image frame in pixels, measured from the stored processed data; record the output pixel dimension after correction and registration.
Height of each corrected image frame in pixels, measured from the stored processed data; record the output pixel dimension after correction and registration.
Number of frames, slices, or projections retained in the corrected and aligned image stack after processing; record the total count in the stored output data object.
Indicates whether registration/alignment was successfully applied to the raw image stack to generate this processed signal artifact.

Basic technical quality flag for the corrected and aligned image output, indicating whether the processed artifact is usable, partially affected by residual artifacts, or failed processing before downstream analysis.
Storage location or URI of the corrected and aligned image file, for example a filesystem path, object-store URI, or database reference used to retrieve the processed data artifact.

structural_segmentation.reasoning: This Process node should describe how the structural features were computed from the corrected images: software identity, version, repository, segmentation algorithm, key parameters, and any processing run controls relevant to reproducing the computation. I excluded properties of the corrected input images because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the output measurement table itself because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided microscope or radiation details because those are outside the semantic territory of this computational process. No already_generated fields were repeated or semantically duplicated.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to perform segmentation and quantification of organelles and cytoskeletal features from the corrected images; record the exact analysis application used in this process.
Version of the analysis software used for structural segmentation; record the installed release or build that generated the feature quantification results.

Repository, package source, or distribution location for the segmentation software; record the source used to identify or reproduce the analysis environment, such as a Git URL, package registry, or vendor site.
Algorithm or model used to identify organelles and cytoskeletal features from the corrected images, such as thresholding, watershed, classical machine learning, or deep learning segmentation.
Name or identifier of the segmentation model used, when a pretrained or custom model was applied; use a string such as a model label or checkpoint name.
Any preprocessing applied immediately before segmentation on the corrected images, such as denoising, normalization, or background subtraction, when performed as part of this computational process.
Numeric threshold or decision cutoff used by the segmentation method, if applicable; record the value used by the algorithm, with units or scale defined by the software implementation.
Minimum connected component or object size retained during segmentation, measured in pixels; record the filter size used to exclude small artifacts from quantified structures.
Set of structural classes or labels produced by the segmentation step, describing which organelle or cytoskeletal categories were quantified in this process.
Indicates whether the segmentation was run on single images or in batch mode across multiple corrected image files.

cellular_structure_metrics.reasoning: This Derivative node should describe the computed result of the segmentation workflow: what quantitative metrics were produced, how many objects or cells were analyzed, and the basic quality of the derived measurement table. I excluded raw and processed image file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal nodes, and I excluded segmentation software and algorithm settings because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also avoided radiation treatment, sample identity, and microscope configuration because those are already represented elsewhere in the DAG. No already_generated fields were repeated or semantically duplicated.

md_schema.descr: File or table format of the derived structural metrics output, such as CSV, TSV, Parquet, or HDF5, as stored after computation; record the actual format used for the derivative artifact.
Total size of the structural metrics output file in bytes at the time of storage; record the archived size of the derived table or measurement file.
Number of segmented cells, organelles, or structural objects included in the quantitative analysis that generated this derivative table; count the objects used to compute the reported metrics.
Number of cells contributing to the derived structural measurements, if cell-level quantification was performed; record the sample size used for the aggregated metrics.

Names of the quantitative structural metrics contained in the output table, such as organelle area, perimeter, shape index, cytoskeletal density, or colocalization scores; provide the metric set produced by this analysis.
Units associated with the derived structural metrics, such as pixels, micrometers, counts, percent, or arbitrary units; specify the unit system used in the output table.
Type of summary statistic represented in the derivative output, if the table aggregates across objects or cells; for example mean, median, standard deviation, or coefficient of variation.
Overall technical quality flag for the derived structural metrics table, indicating whether the computation completed successfully and whether the output is usable for downstream interpretation.
Storage location or URI of the derived structural metrics file, for example a filesystem path, object-store URI, or database reference used to retrieve the quantified results.
